definition: Removing unimportant weights or structures from a trained network to shrink it, exploiting the observation that many parameters contribute little.
details: Removing unimportant weights or structures from a trained network to shrink it, exploiting the observation that many parameters contribute little.

explainer.lead: Network pruning removes unimportant weights or structures from a trained network to shrink it, exploiting the observation that many parameters contribute little.

tiers.eli5: It is like trimming a hedge: you cut the parts that barely do anything so what is left is smaller and easier to handle.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers prune a trained network to reduce its size, relying on the fact that many parameters contribute little. A pitfall is judging importance poorly, since removing the wrong weights harms accuracy.
tiers.paperLevel: Removal of unimportant weights or structures from a trained network to shrink it, based on the observation that many parameters contribute little.

explainer.example: A trained network is pruned by deleting weights judged unimportant, yielding a smaller model.
